div.l: But now is tyme to ȝow for to telle
How þat we beren vs þat ilke nyght
Whan we were in þat Osterye a light
And aft̉er wil I telle of oure viage
And alle þᵉ remnant of oure pylgrymage
But fyrst I pray ȝow of ȝore curtesie
That ȝe ne ret it nought my vylenye
Thow þat I plenly speke in þis mater
To tellen ȝow here wordes ⁊and here chere
Ne thoughe I speke her wordes ꝓproperly
For þis ȝe knowen as welle as I
Who so shal tellen a tale aft̉er a man
He moote reherce as neyghe as eủere he kan
Eủeriche a · werd if it be in his charge
Al speke he neủere so rudele and large
Or elles he moote telle his tale vntrewe
Or feyne þinges of fynde wordes newe
He may not spare al þoughe he were his brother
He mote also welle seiȝe o word as an other
Crist spake hym · self ful brode in holy writte
And welle ȝe wote no vileynye is it
Eke plato seithe ho so kan hym rede
The wordes mote be Cosyne to þᵉ dede
Also I pray ȝow for ȝeue it me
Alle haue I not sette foelke in her degre
Here in þis tale as þᵗat þei shold stonde
My wytte is short ȝe may wel vnderstonde
Greete chere made oure ost vs eủerychon
And to þe Soper sette he vs a noon
He serued vs with vitailles atte þᵉ beste
Strong was þᵉ wyn and welle drink vs leste
A · semely man oure ooste was withe alle
For to ben an Marchall in an halle
A · large man he was with eyen stepe
A · fairer burges is noon in chepe
Bold of his speche and wis ⁊and welle I taught
And of manhode hym lakkid riȝt nouȝt
Eke þerto he was riȝt a mery man
